executiveSummary: GM0794's 2025 identity, boundary, population, neighbourhood, settlement and safety-region inputs reconcile, and the deterministic gate covers all ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Release remains correction-required. The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset gives inland Helmond an internal flood field of 0.557514, 16,786 affected people-equivalent and the same hazard/service state from T+24 through T+72 without a selected major-river source, water level, defence state or connected LIWO footprint. Official local evidence instead distinguishes limited overbank flooding along the Goorloop, Bakelse Aa and Nieuwe Aa from pluvial road/tunnel failure, canal and regional-water operations. The pluvial result is likewise not driven by Helmond's published climate-stress locations or drainage state. Seven materially nonzero hazards reuse exactly the same complete 44-neighbourhood order. A controlled Warandebos source inside Stiphout-Dorp yields direct fire 0.593300 and smoke 0.616915, yet the source neighbourhood ranks tenth. The five-edge road graph, four stations and schedules are useful skeletons but do not establish local crossing, tunnel, hospital, industrial-site, responder or supply access. Public water assets and observations, Elkerliek acute-care context, antennas, schools and one grid-planning sample do not establish live topology, occupancy, capacity, backup or restoration. Keep public context and arithmetic, but suppress exact local hazard, access, outage and recovery claims unless publisher, version, valid time, coverage, licence, evidence class and Unknown/NoData are explicit.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0794 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood and place geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; PDOK inputs retrieved 31 August-3 September 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0794 as Helmond and reports 96,551 residents, density 1,816/km², 18.5% aged 65 or older and 15,886 one-person households; the generated centre is inside the 2025 boundary.

Forty-four published neighbourhood rows sum to 96,530 residents, 21 below the municipality total (-0.022%); households sum to 43,930 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 17,865. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 96,551 without rewriting observations.

One active BAG woonplaats is named Helmond. BRT supplies thirteen settlement labels: one woonkern, six deelkernen, four buurtschappen and two gehuchten; duplicate Kruisschot labels require identity/context handling rather than fabricated population.

CBS neighbourhoods and registered residents are annual administrative context, not hydraulic catchments, utility zones or event-time people. BAG/PDOK place data carries Public Domain Mark 1.0; null, suppressed and not-applicable values remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaatstresstest — Effect van klimaat in de stad
evidenceSources.edition: Current public page and linked climate-stress material inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality says roughly 32 roads or tunnels can become impassable under a large rain event, including the Henri Dunanttunnel, Stiphout streets, Wethouder Ebbenlaan, part of N279 in Dierdonk and locations in Rijpelberg; water nuisance also occurs at rail underpasses.

The municipality distinguishes overbank flooding along Goorloop, Bakelse Aa and Nieuwe Aa and calls Helmond's overall flood risk limited. It identifies heat in the centre and Hoogeind/BZOB, near N270/Zuid-Willemsvaart, in 't Hout and Helmond-Noord, and drought sensitivity in Warandebos.

This is authoritative local screening and planning evidence, not an event-valid rainfall grid, sewer state, live route closure, physical depth, probability or forecast. The page does not state a fixed machine refresh cadence, complete NoData contract or blanket reusable dataset licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Helmond / Waterschap Aa en Maas
evidenceSources.title: Local climate measures, Aa-dal operations and BZOB wastewater investigation
evidenceSources.edition: Official 2021-2026 project and operational pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Aa en Maas found that rainfall sends more wastewater and rainwater to the BZOB sewer pump than it was designed for, causing diluted wastewater to enter the BZOB singel and Rochadevijver; increasing pump capacity was identified as the main measure. A proposed measure is not completed capacity without commissioning evidence.

Municipal pages document completed 2021 Eikendreef drainage works and separate current/planned measures at Odulfusstraat, Park Brouwhuis and other sites. Project-valid dates must be preserved rather than applied citywide.

During the January 2024 high-water operation, Aa en Maas used Diesdonk and other storage, adjusted canal/Aa routing and linked lower Zuid-Willemsvaart discharge to resuming navigation. This demonstrates time-dependent, cross-boundary water, control and mobility state, not a permanent scenario.

Aa en Maas lists Helmond wastewater among flows treated at Aarle-Rixtel and describes a wider network of pumps, transport mains and treatment sites. This establishes an external dependency class, not current flow, spare capacity, quality, power backup or failover. Narrative pages do not expose one reusable topology/licence contract.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning stress test, not a KNMI, WMCN/LIWO, Aa en Maas, RWS, VRBZO, municipality, hospital or operator warning, forecast, probability, evacuation order, casualty model or restoration commitment.

No expert-selected Helmond Rhine/Meuse/IJssel, Goorloop, Bakelse/Nieuwe/Stadse Aa, Zuid-Willemsvaart, regional-water, groundwater, sewer or pluvial scenario with connected footprint drives the simulation.

The current river field is an internal diagnostic, not verified metres; source, hydrograph/datum, defence/control, arrival, velocity, duration/recession, resolution, units, coverage, NoData, uncertainty and layer licence are absent.

Municipal climate screening identifies relevant hotspots but is not an event-valid reusable depth raster, live passability layer or current sewer model; missing raster cells/technical metadata remain Unknown.

Completed, planned and current works are location/date-specific. Eikendreef 2021 measures, BZOB pump enlargement, Park Brouwhuis and Stadse Aa plans cannot be generalized or presumed complete/current without commissioning evidence.
CBS generalized polygons and labels do not resolve terrain, water compartments, sewers, buildings, paving, shade, vegetation, facilities, corridors or household exposure.
CBS values are rounded/suppressed; district-heating and charging are absent everywhere and other fields are partly missing. Null is Unknown, never zero service, demand or safety.

Registered residents omit patients, hospital staff/visitors, industrial workers, pupils, station passengers, commuters, responders and recreational/event visitors; no authorized event-time transient ledger is available.
TOP10NL Warandebos land cover is static eligibility only; the focused ignition is synthetic and no live fuel, moisture, perimeter, wind, access, firewater or suppression state is available.

Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS geometry/schedules do not establish live road/tunnel/canal bridge/rail/bus, evacuation, emergency-priority or freight state and capacity; consecutive corridor edges are non-additive.
Zero covered NDW situations is no usable report at publication time, not proof roads or crossings are open. Water-driven local failures documented by the municipality may fall outside that snapshot.

HWH asset points and project pages do not establish full water/wastewater topology, compatible capacity units, control logic, operation, power backup, staff or repair; absent DAMO points are not absent infrastructure.
Eight Waterinfo records are dated local point measurements from a non-mission-critical public service; they are not citywide thresholds, forecasts, connected inundation or operating instructions.

No complete public physical Enexis feeder/switching, Brabant Water pipe/pressure/quality, gas district/valve, telecom backhaul or municipal sewer topology is authorized in the model; one postcode sample is planning context only.
Elkerliek questionnaire capacity is dated context, not live acceptance, staffing, occupancy, medicines, oxygen, generator/fuel endurance, water/sanitation or restoration.
RDI and DUO points identify registered installation/use, not communications coverage, shelter activation, people present, capacity, supplies, power backup or recovery; RDI reuse terms are unresolved.

Industrial and hazardous-transport source classes do not imply a release. No current complete REV/permit inventory, material, containment, plume, firefighting-water, shutdown or restart state drives the model.
Cyber disruption has no named target, architecture, attack/detection/containment state or authoritative operational evidence; generic service loss is not an observed incident.
No validated inventory is available for crisis reception, pumps/generators, fuel, food/water/medicine stocks, crews, vehicles, mutual aid, household preparedness or completed actions.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not customer outage-hours, injuries, mortality, evacuation, displacement or welfare loss; 72 hours excludes prolonged contamination and reconstruction.
